FunMel

From fungal confrontation photographs to matched-control results.

FunMel measures the colour, shape and melanization index of approximately round Zymoseptoria tritici colonies surrounding another fungus. It separates central fungal tissue and hyphal growth from the target colonies. The outlines can be irregular; photographs do not establish species identity.

Melanization index (MI) is 100 - CIELAB L*. Larger values mean darker tissue. This is an image-darkness proxy, not a direct measurement of melanin concentration.

Install 

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel")
library(FunMel)

Restart R before updating a loaded package. R >= 4.1 and a compilation toolchain are required: Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, matching Rtools on Windows, or R development tools and ImageMagick development libraries on Linux. To install the local vignette:

remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel", build_vignettes = TRUE,
                        dependencies = TRUE)
vignette("FunMel", package = "FunMel")

Start here: prepare, run, finish

No approval columns need to be edited. FunMel prints review reminders and proceeds automatically with valid metadata. Check experimental assignments before processing and inspect image QC before interpreting results. Missing labels, unmatched controls and failed images still need correction.

1. Prepare a photograph folder or ZIP 

project <- prepare_experiment(file.choose(), "FunMel_project")
# Select a ZIP, or replace file.choose() with a photograph-folder path.
project$metadata_file

Use a new project folder. The ZIP may contain nested batches and repeated image basenames; relative paths distinguish files. With folders such as batch_1/control/, batch_1/fungus_A/, batch_2/control/ and batch_2/fungus_B/, the package proposes matching sets and treatment labels. Only explicit control or controls folders denote controls by default. Use control_folders="C" only if that label really means control. A unique plate_metadata.csv inside the input is read automatically; alternatively supply one combined table through metadata=. Ambiguous file names do not establish biological assignments.

Review the printed metadata file. Only correct missing or inaccurate information; there is no confirmation switch. One row represents one independent plate.

Column Meaning
file, relative_file, plate_id Photograph provenance and unique plate identity; preserve these
set_id Treatment plates and their own relevant control plates
treatment control or the actual treatment name
centre_model none for a control; fungus for a central fungus
partner_type Biological partner, normally none or fungus
day, medium, zymo_strain Recorded context; complete and constant within each matching set
replicate, fungus, photo_date, notes Experimental annotations

For one control and three treatment plates, use four rows sharing a set_id. Enter the control once. Four colonies and any sampling spots on a plate are subsamples, not independent biological replicates. Repeated photographs of the same plate are repeated observations, not additional independent plates.

2. Run image analysis 

dish_mm <- 90  # Replace with the verified outer dish diameter (mm).
result <- run_experiment(project, dish_diameter_mm = dish_mm,
                         n_spots = 5, spot_radius_mm = 0.4)
result$analysis_status
result$failed

The diameter is a numeric value, not an interactive prompt. Omit n_spots and spot_radius_mm for whole-colony measurements alone. Spots are additional, deterministically distributed, non-overlapping circular ROIs inside eligible colony tissue. Five spots are requested per colony in this example; they are not five independent replicates. Choose settings consistently across plates. If spots cannot fit, spot_status="insufficient_space"; achieved ROIs remain available, but the requested spot summary is unavailable.

Inspect the QC PNGs in project$qc_dir: target masks, central fungal tissue and hyphae, spot outlines, scale, shadows, illumination and warnings. Correct measurement problems before interpretation. Informative reminders do not require approval-flag edits. Any failed photographs must be resolved before finalization.

3. Finish and export 

reviewed <- finish_experiment(project)
reviewed$melanization_coefficient

This reads the saved measurements and metadata and exports tables, an assessment RDS and a comparison figure in PDF, SVG and 600-dpi PNG. It does not reprocess photographs or require manual approval. Unconfirmed image QC warns and remains recorded; it does not block the default workflow or automatically approve plates. Different recorded days, strains and media are reported separately in context folders; consult context_index.csv when present.

Understand the outputs

The coefficient is mean(treatment plate MI) / mean(matching control plate MI). A plate’s MI is the equally weighted mean of its target-colony MI_mean values. Each treatment uses only controls in its own set. Values above 1 indicate a darker treatment mean, not a fold increase in melanin concentration.

colonies.csv contains whole-colony MI_min, MI_mean and MI_max for eligible interior pixels. spots.csv contains individual ROI measurements. MI_spot_mean/min/max summarize the individual spot means, not pixel extrema or confidence limits. Default coefficients use whole-colony MI. A prespecified spot-based descriptive analysis can use:

spot_coefficients <- melanization_coefficient(reviewed, response = "MI_spot_mean")

Keep spot and whole-colony results labelled separately. Independent plates are the biological units. One control per set permits descriptive ratios but does not meet the built-in replicated-cell inference guard. Supported mixed-model assessment uses lme4/lmerTest, plate-level random effects and matched-set contrasts. Check design, residuals, convergence and singularity before using p-values. The comparison figure shows between-plate SD, not confidence intervals; ratio SD does not include uncertainty in a shared control mean.

Follow eight real photographs

The vignette and examples/walkthrough_14_days.R use eight original photographs: A60_2 and B20_2, each with one control and three confrontation plates. No separate download is required. The combined metadata is supplied, so the example runs without approval-column editing. Verify labels against laboratory records and use the actual dish diameter for scientific interpretation.

vignette("FunMel", package = "FunMel")

The original JPEGs are unchanged. Precomputed tables are illustrative results with a 90-mm scale, max_dim=1200, five 0.4-mm-radius spots and n_boot=20; see extdata/14_day_example/PROVENANCE.md. They are not biological ground truth.

Try one simulated image 

sim <- simulate_plate(width = 400, height = 400, seed = 1)
x <- analyze_plate(sim$image, n_spots = 3, spot_radius_mm = 0.4,
                   n_boot = 20, verbose = FALSE)
plot_qc(x)
x$colonies[, c("colony_id", "MI_min", "MI_mean", "MI_max", "MI_spot_mean")]

For a control, use layout=plate_layout(centre="none"). Advanced functions analyze_plate(), analyze_plates(), make_metadata(), prepare_photo_archive() and finalize_analysis() remain available.

Metadata, calibration and recovery

Additional metadata columns retain their names and values. The complete table is exported as metadata_used.csv. A collision with a measured column receives a metadata_ prefix in measurement tables; original names remain in the full metadata. An optional recorded qc_pass field starts FALSE and is reset for a new image run, but never needs editing for default calculations.

Entirely unrecorded day/strain/medium columns may remain blank. Once recorded, complete them for all plates and keep each context constant within a set. Do not hide differing experimental contexts to pool incompatible plates.

flat_field=TRUE requests spatial illumination correction. It can be withheld when fitted gains saturate: inspect flat_field_applied, flat_field_status and warnings in plates.csv. Withholding does not establish adequate lighting; matched ratios do not guarantee cancellation of illumination bias.

Resume an existing project without recreating it:

project <- readRDS(file.choose()) # Select the existing project.rds.
reviewed <- finish_experiment(project)

Printing a stored path does not prove that the file exists. Restore missing metadata from the saved edited CSV, or point project$metadata_file to that existing file and save the updated project object. Download cloud files locally. Use result$failed to resolve image errors. The package never invents missing experimental assignments. Reanalysis is necessary if image-layout settings change.

The separate algorithm overview describes the methods and comparison with ImageJ/Fiji. Manual ROI tools remain useful for difficult boundaries; no universal accuracy or speed superiority is claimed.
